<RuleLanguageLinks current="html" languages={[{"id":"html","label":"HTML","href":"/linter/rules/use-vue-consistent-v-slot-style/html/"}]} />

:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.5`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/useVueConsistentVSlotStyle`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has a [**safe**](/linter/#safe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`vue`](/linter/domains#vue)
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`vue/v-slot-style`](https://eslint.vuejs.org/rules/v-slot-style)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useVueConsistentVSlotStyle": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Enforce a consistent style for `v-slot` in Vue templates.

Vue lets you write the same slot in three ways:

- the shorthand `#`, as in `#header`;
- the longhand `v-slot:`, as in `v-slot:header`;
- `v-slot` without a slot name, which only works for the default slot.

Mixing these styles makes templates harder to read. This rule reports slots that
don't use the configured style.

By default, the rule expects:

- `v-slot` for the default slot when it's placed directly on a component, as in
`<MyComponent v-slot="props">`;
- `#default` for the default slot on a `<template>` element;
- `#name` for named slots.

## Examples

### Invalid

```vue
<template>
  <MyComponent #default="data">{{ data }}</MyComponent>
</template>
```

<strong>4</strong> <strong>4</strong><strong> │ </strong>    &lt;/MyComponent&gt;<br />    <strong>5</strong> <strong>5</strong><strong> │ </strong>  &lt;/template&gt;<br />  <br /></code></pre>"} />

### Valid

```vue
<template>
  <MyComponent v-slot="data">{{ data }}</MyComponent>
  <MyComponent>
    <template #default>content</template>
    <template #header>content</template>
  </MyComponent>
</template>
```

## Options

The `atComponent` and `default` options accept `"shorthand"`, `"longhand"`, or
`"v-slot"`. The `named` option accepts `"shorthand"` or `"longhand"`, because a named
slot always needs its name.

- `"shorthand"`: write `#`, as in `#default` or `#header`.
- `"longhand"`: write `v-slot:`, as in `v-slot:default` or `v-slot:header`.
- `"v-slot"`: write `v-slot` without a slot name.

### `atComponent`

Default: `"v-slot"`

The style for the default slot when `v-slot` is placed directly on a component, as in
`<MyComponent v-slot="data">`.

```json title='biome.json'
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useVueConsistentVSlotStyle": {
					"level": "on",
					"options": {
						"atComponent": "shorthand"
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

```

#### Invalid

```vue
<template>
  <MyComponent v-slot="data">{{ data }}</MyComponent>
</template>
```

### `default`

Default: `"shorthand"`

The style for the default slot on a `<template>` element, as in
`<template #default>`.

```json title='biome.json'
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useVueConsistentVSlotStyle": {
					"level": "on",
					"options": {
						"default": "v-slot"
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

```

#### Invalid

```vue
<template>
  <MyComponent>
    <template #default>content</template>
  </MyComponent>
</template>
```

### `named`

Default: `"shorthand"`

The style for named slots, as in `<template #header>`. A slot with a dynamic name,
such as `#[name]`, is a named slot.

```json title='biome.json'
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useVueConsistentVSlotStyle": {
					"level": "on",
					"options": {
						"named": "longhand"
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

```

#### Invalid

```vue
<template>
  <MyComponent>
    <template #header>content</template>
  </MyComponent>
</template>
```
